name: Approval without vote
title: RECOMMENDATION FOR SECOND READING on the Council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety of toys and repealing Directive 2009/48/EC
part_text:
The European Parliament has approved the Council's position on a new law on toy safety, which replaces an older 2009 directive. The text itself does not spell out the detailed rules. It also notes a Commission promise: the Commission will ask the European Chemicals Agency to review the safety of certain chemicals in toys — nitrosamines and related substances within 12 months, and lead, cadmium, mercury and chromium within 24 months of the law taking effect. The law is now adopted.

- The law on toy safety is adopted, replacing the 2009 rules; the detailed content is not described here.
- It affects toy makers and sellers, and children who play with toys across the EU.
- The Commission will ask its chemicals agency to review limits for certain substances in toys.
